content.user_title: Review Letters of Credit and Trade Finance
content.value_statement: Cross-border teams need clear analysis of credit terms, financing choices, clearing routes, and authenticity risks. This skill provides structured reviews and compliant recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Explains common MT700 fields and identifies documentary requirements, deadlines, and soft clauses.
Compares negotiation, factoring, two-factor factoring, and forfaiting against term and risk-transfer needs.
Outlines CIPS and SWIFT clearing routes with key message-mapping considerations.
Reviews whether UCP600 or ISP98 is relevant to the proposed instrument.
Structures trade-background and receivables-authenticity checks before financing analysis.
Outlines compliant ABS, ABN, or licensed offshore tokenization paths for genuine trade assets.
limitations: It does not replace advice from banks, lawyers, regulators, auditors, or licensed financial institutions.
It cannot verify documents, counterparties, ownership, sanctions status, or transaction authenticity without reliable evidence.
Its regulatory references may not reflect changes after the knowledge base date.
It does not issue, amend, authenticate, transmit, or settle financial messages.

use_cases.title: Review Export Credit Terms
use_cases.description: Assess MT700 terms, required documents, deadlines, discrepancies, and soft clauses before an exporter accepts the credit.

use_cases.title: Select a Financing Structure
use_cases.description: Compare negotiation, factoring, two-factor factoring, and forfaiting for a genuine receivable and defined risk-transfer objective.

use_cases.title: Design a Clearing and Compliance Review
use_cases.description: Outline CIPS or SWIFT routing, message mapping, foreign-exchange checks, and data-transfer review points.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an MT700 Field
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain MT700 field [field code] in simple terms. Describe its purpose, common values, and one practical review question.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the purpose of a single documentary credit field.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Financing Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare negotiation, factoring, two-factor factoring, and forfaiting for this transaction: [details]. State assumptions, suitability, risk transfer, and required evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a financing approach for a genuine cross-border receivable.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Letter of Credit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these MT700 terms: [terms]. Identify deadlines, document requirements, inconsistencies, soft clauses, UCP600 issues, missing information, and questions for the issuing bank.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a structured review before accepting or amending a credit.

prompt_templates.title: Design an End-to-End Trade Finance Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a trade finance plan for [transaction]. Start with authenticity checks, then cover instrument choice, clearing, message mapping, compliance, controls, and handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop a complete cross-border structure with explicit controls and professional review points.

output_examples.input: Compare factoring and forfaiting for a two-year export receivable supported by an accepted bill.
output: Precondition: confirm the sale, receivable, acceptance, ownership, and absence of duplicate financing.
Forfaiting is generally better aligned with a medium-term, non-recourse risk transfer objective.
Factoring is stronger when ongoing receivables administration and shorter-term portfolio financing are required.
Obtain bank, legal, sanctions, and jurisdiction-specific review before commitment.

output_examples.input: Review a credit that expires before the latest shipment date and requires a buyer-issued inspection certificate.
output: Critical inconsistency: expiry before shipment prevents a compliant presentation under the stated timetable.
Soft-clause risk: the buyer controls issuance of the inspection certificate and could prevent presentation.
Recommended action: request an amendment to extend expiry and replace the buyer-controlled certificate with an independent document.

output_examples.input: Outline controls for converting SWIFT trade instructions into a CIPS clearing workflow.
output: Confirm currency, participant status, settlement route, and applicable foreign-exchange reporting.
Map amount, currency, value date, party identifiers, bank identifiers, and transaction references.
Use reconciliation, dual approval, exception handling, and message-version checks before release.

best_practices: Provide complete instrument terms, transaction facts, jurisdictions, currencies, dates, and supporting evidence.
Treat trade-background authenticity and receivable ownership as prerequisites for every financing recommendation.
Confirm current rules and final structures with relevant banks, lawyers, regulators, and licensed specialists.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to create, alter, or conceal documents to obtain financing.
Do not treat illustrative field mappings as production-ready payment or messaging instructions.
Do not rely on the skill as the sole source for legal, regulatory, sanctions, tax, or credit decisions.

faq.question: Can this skill issue or amend a letter of credit?
faq.answer: No. It can analyze terms and suggest questions, but only authorized financial institutions can issue or amend the instrument.

faq.question: Does it support MT700 reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains major fields, documentary requirements, dates, soft clauses, and potential inconsistencies.

faq.question: Can it choose between factoring and forfaiting?
faq.answer: It can compare suitability based on tenor, recourse, risk transfer, and receivables management. A licensed provider must approve the final structure.

faq.question: Can it design a CIPS clearing route?
faq.answer: It can outline routes and mapping considerations. Participating banks must validate current message standards, access, reporting, and settlement details.

faq.question: Does it verify that a trade is genuine?
faq.answer: No. It provides a review framework, but verification requires reliable documents, independent checks, and accountable professional judgment.

faq.question: Can it advise on trade finance asset tokenization?
faq.answer: It can outline high-level compliant paths and restrictions. Legal, licensing, ownership, investor, and jurisdictional reviews remain mandatory.
